summary: On a member that trims locally and sets [trim] mail = true, closed agent and daemon mail in the graph now retires a week after it closes: all of a thread's message.* claims are deleted, their IDs join the retired set, and the freed pages go back to the filesystem. Person threads and any thread another claim cites are kept forever. This replaces the 2026-10-30 decision C15 (keep all messages forever) for non-person mail. On a copy of a real 58.9 GB member, the first pass retired 490,235 claims in 99,732 threads and gave 2.07 GB (3.5%) back to the filesystem; a member frees roughly the share of its graph that closed agent and daemon mail holds, plus that mail's replica, signature and verdict rows. Later passes retire about a day's closed mail each. It is off unless set: whether it becomes the default for members that trim locally is the owner's decision, still open.

replay.detail: A retired thread's claims leave this member's graph and their IDs enter retired_claim_ids in the deleting transaction, through the trim's own delete path (replica record, operation, event, signature and verdict rows, and every projection's delete trigger). The rule reads only claims, so every trim-local member retires the same threads with no coordination; peers compare the retained and retired sets, and admission refuses a retired ID, so none comes back.

schema.detail: No table, index or trigger change. Two meta keys: mail_retirement_closed_through (how far closed threads have been judged) and mail_retirement_deferred (a JSON list, at most 1,024, of threads judged before their sent claim arrived, judged again by later steps).

rules.detail: Retention of graph mail on trim-local members with [trim] mail = true: message.* claims of a closed thread whose sender and recipient are not persons and that no other claim cites retire seven days after its message.closed was accepted. Members that do not trim locally, or do not set [trim] mail = true, keep everything as before. Mail in the messages shard is not touched.

compatibility.detail: Mixed versions: an older member keeps its copies and never retires; it already holds what a retiring member no longer serves, and the retiring member's admission refuses those IDs, so replication stays whole (fleet::previous_release_beside_a_member_that_retires_closed_mail_and_its_rollback). A previous release refuses the [trim] mail key: set it only after upgrading, and remove it before rolling back.

downtime.detail: No migration. The daemon retires in its own task, starting 10-15 minutes after start, one writer hold of at most 40 ms at a time with a rest of four times the hold, and gives free pages back 128 at a time. Measured on that copy with builds running on the host (load 3 to 18), over 8,080 holds: retirement holds p50 46 ms, p99 63 ms, max 412 ms, 0.59% over 100 ms; the smallest ordinary write (one meta row at the member's normal level) in the same run p50 25 ms, p99 341 ms, max 11.0 s, 6.6% over 100 ms. Free-page steps of 128 pages: p50 9 ms, p99 97 ms, max 1.5 s. The longest holds are the host's disk stalls, which every writer sees.

manual.detail: To turn it on, set [trim] mail = true on a member that trims locally, after upgrading; remove the key before rolling back to a previous release.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release keeps working: it reads the smaller store, its retired ledger is the same authority and refuses the retired IDs (verified by the fleet test above). Retired mail does not come back on a rollback. Remove [trim] mail before rolling back: the previous release refuses the key. Retirement steps and free-page steps commit at synchronous=NORMAL with no checkpoint inside the commit; the pragmas are put back around exactly those commits, on error too, so every other write keeps the member's own level. A crash or power loss can lose only the last retirement steps since the writer's previous ordinary commit; their claims are still there and the next pass retires them again.
